documents.issuer: NC DHHS, Division of Health Service Regulation, Mental Health Licensure & Certification Section (Licensure & Training team)
documents.how_used: This is the primary source of required_items. It is the DHSR checklist that the Licensure & Training reviewer uses to check the written P&P manual (items 1-93, pages 2-27). The provider enters the manual page number for each item and marks Yes/No. Not every item applies to a Supervised Living 'C' home, so a few are marked conditional below.

documents.how_used: This is the submission-order checklist for the program review. It tells the provider to 'Submit documents in the same order as listed.' I took only the policy and plan items from it: the P&P manual and worksheet, the training requirements and curriculum, and the written disaster plan with Emergency Management verification. The staff records, instructor credentials and NCID items are excluded as paperwork.

documents.title: Initial Licensure Application Packet
documents.issuer: NC DHHS DHSR Mental Health Licensure & Certification Section
documents.how_used: Process document only. It says to develop written P&Ps for the service and 'DO NOT SEND Policies and Procedures with this application'; they are reviewed later by the Licensure & Training team. It also lists the rule subchapters the P&Ps must be built from. No required_items come from it, because the rest is application paperwork.

documents.issuer: NC DHHS DHSR Mental Health Licensure & Certification Section
documents.how_used: Describes how the program review works: the manual and worksheet are submitted, staff must be hired before licensure, a walk-through is done, and the disaster plan is reviewed by the county Emergency Management office. It lists no policy items of its own.

required_items.text: Procedure defining delegation of management authority for the agency's operation and services (chain of command).
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0201 Governing Body Policies; Worksheet p.2

required_items.text: Procedure for criteria for discharge of the client from the facility/agency: reasons a client might be discharged, and the notice period and recipients of the notice.

Procedure on Client Record Management: transportation of records, safeguarding against loss, tampering and defacement, authorized-user access at all times, confidentiality, and providing access to information for clients.
Procedure with guidelines for safe transportation of clients, tailored to individual needs, including securing and accessing emergency information in transit.

Procedures on the composition and activities of a QA/QI committee. Activities include: monitoring and evaluating quality of care, outcomes and service utilization; a written QA/QI plan; professional/clinical supervision by a qualified professional; strategies for improving care; review of staff qualifications and granting of treatment/habilitation privileges; review of all fatalities of active clients in area-operated or contracted residential programs; and adoption of operational and programmatic performance standards.
Procedures for reporting Level I, II and III incidents, including specific measures to prevent similar incidents and how the agency will implement IRIS (Incident Response Improvement System).

Client Fee Assessment and Collection Procedure: how clients or legal representatives are informed of all fees for assessment, treatment and habilitation, and practices for assessing and collecting fees.
Procedures for the agency's medical preparedness plan and how it will be used in a medical emergency.
Procedures on use of volunteers: whether used, services provided, training, supervisor, and how client confidentiality is ensured.
Policy on training for professional and paraprofessional staff: what training is provided and how ongoing staff education is ensured.
Policy on identifying, reporting, investigating and controlling infectious and communicable diseases affecting staff and clients, including training on infectious diseases and blood-borne pathogens.

Policy on implementing and documenting an individualized supervision plan for all paraprofessional staff upon hire. It must specify who develops the plan, the staff's areas of need and methods to address them, and that the plan is reviewed and signed by both staff member and supervisor.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0204 Competencies and Supervision of Paraprofessionals; Worksheet p.4

required_items.text: Admission and Assessment policy: procedure for an admission assessment before services, including presenting problem, needs and strengths, provisional/admitting diagnosis with an established diagnosis within 30 days, social/family/medical history, evaluations appropriate to needs, and documented strategies when services start before the plan is in place.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0205 Assessment and Treatment/Habilitation or Service Plan; Worksheet pp.4-5

required_items.text: Policy on developing a treatment/habilitation plan within 30 days of admission (or before, if applicable), with the client and/or legally responsible person. It must include anticipated outcomes with projected dates, strategies, responsible staff, an at-least-annual review schedule, the basis for evaluating outcomes, and written consent or a written statement of why consent was not obtained.

Emergency Plans and Supplies policy: a written fire safety plan for each facility and an area-wide disaster plan approved by the appropriate local authority; plans accessible to staff and evacuation procedures/routes posted; fire and disaster drills at least quarterly in 24-hour facilities, repeated for each shift; drills simulating actual fire emergencies; basic first aid supplies available.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0207 Emergency Plans and Supplies; Worksheet pp.5-6

required_items.text: The P&P manual documents that the agency chooses NOT to administer medications, and that it will not prescribe, handle, dispense, administer, transport, dispose of or store medications. Complete only if the home does not handle medications.

Medication Dispensing procedure: dispensing only by a registered pharmacist, physician or other person authorized by law and registered with the NC Board of Pharmacy; only on a written order from a licensed M.D.; no stock of prescription drugs for dispensing except in emergencies without hiring a pharmacist; take-home methadone by R.N.s only (applies only to programs licensed to distribute methadone).
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0209, Medication Dispensing Procedures; Worksheet p.6

required_items.text: Medication Packaging and Labeling procedures: manufacturer's label and visible expiration date on non-prescription containers not dispensed by a pharmacist; tamper-resistant packaging for prescriptions (including samples); prescription labels showing client name, prescriber, dispensing date, directions, drug name/strength/quantity/expiration, and pharmacy or dispensing location details and dispensing practitioner.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0209, Medication Packaging and Labeling Procedures; Worksheet p.7

required_items.text: Medication Administration procedures: administration only on a written order from a legally authorized prescriber; self-administration only if authorized in writing by the physician; administration by licensed personnel or unlicensed staff trained by an R.N., pharmacist or other qualified professional; a current MAR for each client, documented immediately after administration (client name, drug name/strength/quantity, instructions, date and time, name or initials of administering person); client requests for medication changes documented and filed with the MAR, followed by physician consultation.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0209, Medication Administration Procedures; Worksheet pp.7-8

required_items.text: Medication Disposal procedures: disposal to prevent diversion or accidental ingestion; a disposal record (client, drug, strength, quantity, date and method, signature of the person disposing and the witness); methods for non-controlled substances (incineration, flushing into septic/sewer, or transfer to a local pharmacy); remaining medication disposed of promptly or held no more than 30 days after discharge unless the client is expected to return.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0209, Medication Disposal Procedures; Worksheet p.8

required_items.text: Medication Storage procedures: a securely locked cabinet in a clean, well-lit, ventilated room at 59-86 degrees F; refrigerator at 36-46 degrees F, with medications in a separate locked compartment if food is also stored; separate storage for each client and for external vs. internal use; secure storage if a physician approves self-medication.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0209, Medication Storage Procedures; Worksheet pp.8-9

required_items.text: Medication Review procedure: 6-month drug review by a physician or pharmacist for clients on psychotropic medications; findings and any corrective action recorded in the client record.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0209, Medication Review Procedures; Worksheet p.9

required_items.text: Medication Error procedures: how errors and significant adverse drug reactions are reported immediately to the client's physician or pharmacist, and how a client's refusal of medication is documented.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0209, Medication Errors Procedures; Worksheet p.9

required_items.text: Search and Seizure policy: conditions for searching a client or living space, including procedures for seizing belongings or property in the client's possession.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27D .0103 Search and Seizure Policy; Worksheet p.9

required_items.text: The search and seizure policy documents that clients will be free from unwarranted invasion of privacy.

The policy states every search and seizure is documented, including scope of search, reason, procedures followed, description of any property seized, and an account of the disposition of seized property.
Policy on how the governing body ensures a compliance review of Client Rights Rules implementation at least every 3 years, with the 3 most recent written review reports kept.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27D .0104 Periodic Internal Review; Worksheet p.10

required_items.text: Informing Clients policy: written summary of rights (G.S. 122C Art. 3) to client and legally responsible person; right to contact Disability Rights NC; timely notification (24-hour facilities within 72 hours, explained at the client's level of understanding); information to be provided (rules and penalties, confidentiality protections G.S. 122C-52 through 56, how to get a copy of the treatment/habilitation plan, and governing body policies on fee assessment/collection, grievance procedures with contact info and assistance, suspension and expulsion, and search and seizure); special considerations for restrictive interventions and restricted rights (behavior management systems, potential restrictions, notification after emergency use, notification of legally responsible persons, notification of rights restrictions); documentation in the client record that rights were fully explained.

Informing Staff policy: how staff are informed about Client Rights and how documentation is maintained, plus a procedure requiring each staff member to sign an acknowledgment of receipt, kept on file.

Social Integration policy (day/night or 24-hour facilities): guidelines for encouraging and facilitating appropriate social interaction among clients and with community non-clients. It covers encouragement of participation, no prohibition of social interaction unless a written restriction is in the client record, and what counts as appropriate interactions.

Client Self-Governance policy (day/night or 24-hour facilities): client input in facility governance with mechanisms for feedback; development of client self-governance groups; meeting and communication protocols between clients and staff; training and support for clients and staff.

Informed Consent policy: informing clients about benefits, risks, alternatives, length of consent validity and withdrawal procedures (consent for planned restrictive intervention not to exceed six months); written consent per G.S. 122C-57(f) or Subchapter 27E .0100 planned interventions, and for drugs such as Antabuse and Depo-Provera when used for non-FDA-approved uses; right to consent or refuse under G.S. 122C-57(d), with refusal not used as the sole ground for termination except as stated; documentation of informed consent in the client record.

Protection From Harm, Abuse, Neglect or Exploitation policy: protection from harm per G.S. 122C-66; definitions and prohibition of abuse and neglect per 10A NCAC 27C .0102; transaction policies on sale or purchase of goods or services involving clients; use of force guidelines; employee conduct repercussions including dismissal; staff training on recognizing, preventing and reporting; documentation and reporting procedures.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27D .0304 Protection From Harm, Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation; Worksheet p.14

required_items.text: Least Restrictive Alternative policy: services delivered in the least restrictive and most appropriate settings and methods; promotion of coping and engagement skills; meaningful activity choices; shared decision-making; restrictive interventions only as a last resort, with dignity and respect, by trained personnel.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27E .0101 Least Restrictive Alternative; Worksheet p.15

required_items.text: Prohibited Procedures policy: clear prohibition of banned interventions, including corporal punishment (G.S. 122C-59), contingent painful body contact, substances that induce painful bodily reactions (excluding Antabuse), electric shock (excluding medically administered ECT), insulin shock, unpleasant-tasting foodstuffs, contingent noxious substances (noise, bad smells, splashing with water), and any potentially physically painful procedure or stimulus used to reduce a behavior (excluding prescribed injections).
Policy with clear guidelines and procedures for restricting client rights and implementing interventions that ensure safety, dignity and respect; provided to all staff.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27D .0101 Policy on Rights Restrictions and Interventions; Worksheet p.16 (numbered '35a' in the document)

required_items.text: Procedures on how ALL instances of alleged or suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation of clients are documented and reported to the County Department of Social Services.
Procedures and safeguards for prescribing medications that present a serious risk to the client, with special focus on neuroleptic medications.
Identify in the policy any restrictive interventions prohibited from use within the facility.
If the facility operates 24 hours, outline the circumstances and procedures prohibiting staff from restricting a client's rights.
Policy outlining the permitted restrictive interventions and the approved training curriculum; if none are permitted, the policy must explicitly say they are not allowed.
Policy identifies the staff member (position) responsible for informing the client of any restrictions that may be used.
Policy documents that clients who refuse restrictive interventions are afforded due process. (Worksheet pp.16-22: the highlighted items apply if the agency uses restrictive interventions.)
Policy includes the staff position responsible for giving written permission for 24-hour restrictive interventions. (Highlighted; applies if restrictive interventions are used.)
Policy designates the specific staff responsible for review of the use of restrictive interventions. (Highlighted; applies if restrictive interventions are used.)

Policy states what considerations are given to the client's physical and psychological well-being before, during and after a restrictive intervention, including review of health history or a health assessment at admission for pre-existing conditions or limitations that raise risk. (Highlighted; applies if restrictive interventions are used.)

Policy guidelines for debriefing and planning sessions with clients and legally responsible persons to reduce future use: debriefing process, planning process, and documentation/communication to the client and LRP after use. (Highlighted; applies if restrictive interventions are used.)

Policy with guidelines for intervention procedures as therapeutic treatment methods that are clinically or medically justified and authorized by qualified professionals (determination and authorization only by a physician or licensed practicing psychologist formally trained and privileged in the procedure). (Highlighted.)
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27E .0103 General Policies Regarding Intervention Procedures; Worksheet pp.17-18

required_items.text: Policy states that it applies to all staff involved in client care and in implementing restrictive interventions. (Highlighted.)
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27E .0104 Seclusion, Physical Restraint, Isolation Time-Out, and Protective Devices Used for Behavioral Control; Worksheet p.18

required_items.text: Guidelines for the use of seclusion, physical restraint, isolation and protective devices for behavioral management. (Highlighted.)
Procedures outlining limitations on the use of restrictive interventions. (Highlighted.)
Guidelines on prohibited uses, such as coercion, punishment, retaliation, staff convenience or inadequate staffing; interventions must not cause harm or abuse.
Documentation outlining the acceptable use of restrictive interventions within the facility.

Elements for procedures on use of seclusion: positive, less restrictive alternatives tried first; how staff are identified, trained and evaluated for competence; staff responsibilities and professional roles during interventions; documentation and notification protocols after any restrictive intervention; and (continued on p.19) procedures for well-being checks and assessing consequences after the intervention. (Highlighted.)
Guidelines on room requirements for Seclusion and Isolation, if used (DHSR must approve the room).
Guidelines for documenting use of restrictive interventions in client records, including rationale, methods and debriefing. (Highlighted.)
Guidelines for emergency use of restrictive interventions, including time limits and authorization procedures. (Highlighted.)
Guidelines on precautions and actions during restrictive interventions, including continuous monitoring and documentation. (Highlighted.)
Procedures for discontinuing restrictive interventions at any indication of risk to health or safety or once the client gains behavioral control. (Highlighted.)

Notification within 24 hours of the treatment/habilitation team or designee after each use, a governing body designee, and immediate notification of the legally responsible person of a minor or incompetent adult unless they asked not to be notified. (Highlighted.)

Review and Reporting procedures: review time frame set by a governing body designee and the Client Rights Committee, with confidentiality; investigation of unusual or possibly unwarranted patterns of use; a log of client name, responsible professional, date/time/type, duration and reason, alternatives considered and why not used, debriefing and planning with client/LRP/staff, and adverse effects. (Highlighted.)
The agency's data collection and analysis procedures on the use of seclusion and physical restraint. (Highlighted.)
The agency's procedures if planned intervention is used. (Highlighted.)

Protective Devices procedure: necessity for the device; employee using it is trained and competent; observation and interventions documented in the client record; protocol for maintenance and cleaning.

Procedure documenting that, if the facility is operated by or under contract with an area program, use of protective devices in the treatment/habilitation plan is subject to Client Rights Committee review.
An Intervention Advisory Committee shall be established for additional safeguards in a facility that uses restrictive interventions as planned interventions. (Highlighted.)
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27E .0106 Intervention Advisory Committee; Worksheet p.20

required_items.text: Document who is required to join the agency's Intervention Advisory Committee. (Highlighted.)
Procedure governing the Intervention Advisory Committee, detailing how client information is disseminated and the reasoning for it. (Highlighted.)
Procedure documenting the specific training and orientation given to the Intervention Advisory Committee. (Highlighted.)

Policy documents that all staff, service providers, employees, students and volunteers involved in client care must be trained in approved de-escalation techniques as alternatives to restrictive interventions.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27E .0107 Training on Alternatives to Restrictive Interventions; Worksheet p.21

required_items.text: Policy documents a formal annual refresher in an approved de-escalation curriculum for all staff.
Procedures for keeping documentation of alternatives-to-restrictive-intervention training for all staff for at least three years (participants, pass/fail outcomes, training dates, instructor names).
Policy documents the instructor's qualifications and training requirements.
Procedures for maintaining documentation of alternatives training and of initial and refresher instructor training for at least three years.
Policy states that any staff using restrictive interventions must be trained and current in an approved restrictive-intervention training program. (Highlighted.)
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27E .0108 Training in Seclusion, Physical Restraint, and Isolation Time-Out; Worksheet p.22

required_items.text: Documentation of the approved curriculum for restrictive interventions used; if none are used, a policy stating the agency will not use restrictive interventions. (Highlighted.)
Show where in the policy the prerequisite training requirements for staff to use restrictive interventions are outlined. (Highlighted.)
Policy documents a formal annual refresher in an approved restrictive intervention, successfully completed by all staff. (Highlighted.)
Policy states that restrictive-intervention instructors must be retrained at least annually and be currently CPR-trained. (Highlighted.)
Procedures for maintaining initial and refresher instructor training documentation for at least three years. (Highlighted.)
Suspension and Expulsion policy states each client shall be free from threat or fear of unwarranted suspension or expulsion from the facility.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27D .0102 Suspension and Expulsion Policy; Worksheet p.22

required_items.text: Policy outlines criteria for suspension, expulsion or other forms of discharge that are not mutually agreed upon.

Policy sets documentation requirements: time frame for resuming services after a suspension; specific conditions and timeline for resuming services; staff efforts to identify alternative services meeting the client's needs, and designation of those services; any necessary discharge plan.

Health Care Personnel Registry policy: the agency's responsibility to vet all unlicensed staff with possible direct access to clients or their property through the HCPR, and how it will handle report-allegation procedures, investigation procedures, submission of investigation results, and documentation requirements.
required_items.cite: G.S. 131E-256 Health Care Personnel Registry (HCPR); Worksheet p.23

required_items.text: Policy on which staff position of a facility for individuals with intellectual disabilities will notify the LME/MCO serving the client's county of residence of the intent to close the facility or discharge a client who may need continuing care, at least 60 days before the closure or discharge.
required_items.cite: N.C.G.S. 122C-63 Continuity of Care; Worksheet p.23 (the document numbers this '84')

required_items.text: Policy documenting that every client in a 24-hour facility receives necessary treatment for physical ailments, with guidelines on the right to necessary treatment, the right to an individualized discharge plan, and unanticipated discontinuation of treatment.
required_items.cite: N.C.G.S. 122C-61 Treatment Rights in 24-hour Facilities; Worksheet p.24 (the document also numbers this '84', so the id here is disambiguated)

required_items.text: Policy outlining adult clients' rights: confidential phone calls; visitors 8:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. for at least 6 hours daily, 2 after 6:00 p.m., not taking precedence over therapies; communicating and meeting under appropriate supervision with individuals of their choice; visits outside the facility unless commitment or court-order issues; time outdoors daily and access to exercise facilities several times a week; keeping and using personal clothing and possessions; religious worship; retaining a driver's license unless prohibited; individual private storage space.
required_items.cite: N.C.G.S. 122C-62 Additional Rights in 24-hour Facilities; Worksheet p.24

required_items.text: Policy outlining minor clients' rights under G.S. 122C-62 (phone calls, supervised visitors, mail, special education and vocational training, outdoor play and recreation, personal clothing and possessions, religious worship, storage space, spending a reasonable sum of their money, driver's license). Likely not applicable to a 'C' (adult) home, but the worksheet's 'No/N/A' rule requires a comment explaining why.

Living Environment policy: how the agency provides each client a living environment that promotes comfort, privacy and personalization, with guidelines ensuring uninterrupted sleep, personal privacy and the ability to personalize living space.

Health, Hygiene and Grooming policy: guidelines for personal health, hygiene and grooming care that respect client rights and dignity, including the right to dignity, privacy and humane care, opportunities for personal hygiene, access to hygiene products, and facilities that ensure privacy.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27F .0103 Health, Hygiene and Grooming; Worksheet pp.25-26

required_items.text: Guidelines and procedures for staff to safeguard clients' personal clothing and possessions: efforts to protect belongings, how employees help clients develop and keep an inventory, and procedures for documenting and monitoring personal belongings.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27F .0104 Storage and Protection of Clothing and Possessions; Worksheet p.26

required_items.text: Client's Personal Funds policy: guidelines for assisting clients with managing and investing personal funds, including assistance with personal fund accounts, management of funds by facility employees, and authorization for deductions.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27F .0105 Client's Personal Funds; Worksheet p.26

required_items.text: Facilities With Pools: policy states any agency pool must be approved by the DHSR Construction Section and includes guidelines on staff supervision and safety measures. Conditional; complete only if there is a pool.
required_items.cite: Worksheet heading 'Facilities With Pools'; Worksheet p.27

required_items.text: Facility Animals: policy that clients, visitors and staff who bring owned dogs, cats and ferrets must have proof of vaccination, with procedures for documenting and verifying rabies vaccination proof and keeping vaccination records for all pets on the premises. Conditional; complete if animals are allowed.

Medication and Mobile Units policy (service provisions, location and service capacity, operations and service delivery). Applies only to medication and mobile units, so not applicable to Supervised Living.
Facility's Policies and Procedures Manual, submitted with the MH Licensure Policies and Procedures Worksheet (first item in the submission order).

notes:
SOURCES AND LIMITS. DHSR's Policy & Procedure Worksheet is the single official checklist for the policy content. It is a general mental-health worksheet that cites 10A NCAC 27G .0200, 27D, 27E, 27F and the statutes. It has no items drawn from the Supervised Living rules (10A NCAC 27G .5601-.5604). I could not retrieve the .5600 rule text itself, so no .5600-specific policy items are listed. Item text above is condensed from the form because of quoting limits; the item numbering and rule cites follow the form, and the PDF has the exact wording. The form numbers two different items '84' (G.S. 122C-63 on p.23 and G.S. 122C-61 on p.24); I disambiguated them with bracketed cites. It also has an item '35a'.

HOW IT IS SUBMITTED. Per the Application Packet, do NOT send the P&Ps with the license application. After the zoning, LME/MCO letter of support, floor plan and photo items are in and DHSR Construction has done the physical plant review, the Licensure & Training team contacts the applicant to begin the program review. The applicant has six months from that first contact to finish it; DHSR describes the manual as the licensee's own and says it is returned for revision if incomplete or incorrect.

WORKSHEET RULES (Submission Guidelines, REV 7-22-25):
- Submit the P&P manual as ONE PDF and the worksheet as a SEPARATE PDF.
- List the exact manual page number for each required policy.
- If you answer 'No' or 'N/A', explain why in the comment box.
- Worksheets must be complete and correct; incomplete or incorrect ones are returned.
- Flowcharts are not accepted as policy documents.
- If the agency uses restrictive interventions, complete the highlighted areas on worksheet pages 16-22. I marked those items '(Highlighted)', but the highlighting is hard to read in the PDF text, so confirm against the PDF.
- The slide deck says the worksheet is a guide, not a substitute for the regulations. The Application Packet says to build the P&Ps from 10A NCAC Ch. 26 Subch. C and Ch. 27 Subchs. C, D, E, F and G.

SUBMISSION ORDER. The Required Materials list says to submit documents in the order listed: P&P manual and worksheet; personnel records; staff training; training curriculum; instructor credentials; disaster plan. The 'Substance Abuse Waiver Training' group applies to SUD services only. A written disaster plan with verification from local Emergency Management is required; the county Emergency Management office confirms in writing that the plan was reviewed.

APPLICABILITY TO A SUPERVISED LIVING 'C' HOME (adult DD, 24-hour residential):
- Item 86 (minors' rights) is likely N/A because the population is adults.
- Item 93 (medication and mobile units) is N/A.
- Items 91 (pools) and 92 (animals) apply only if the home has a pool or allows animals.
- Medication items 17-23 apply if the home handles medications; item 16 is the opt-out statement used only if it does not.
- The restrictive-intervention items (35a-79) apply as written if restrictive interventions are used. If none are used, items 40 and 75 require an explicit statement that they are not allowed.
- Item 84 [G.S. 122C-63] is written for facilities serving individuals with intellectual disabilities, so it applies to a 'C' home.

SEPARATE FROM POLICY CONTENT. Staff records, resumes, license verifications, HCPR and criminal checks, instructor credentials, NCID username, application forms, ownership information, fees, floor plan and photos, zoning letter, LME/MCO letter of support, and the fire and sanitation inspections are paperwork, not policy content. The walk-through checklist is a separate pre-licensure inspection. The slide deck says all staff must be hired and in place before a license is granted.
